nodes.label: Bearer Token Pairing (extension auth)
nodes.rationale: A fetch from a chrome-extension:// page is cross-site and Clerk's session cookie is SameSite=Lax, so the browser never attaches it. Instead /extension mints a token via POST /api/extension/token, posts it to its own window, connect.js relays it to the worker, and it lands in chrome.storage.local for Authorization: Bearer calls. The API still accepts session cookies too, so the endpoints keep working from a signed-in tab and can move to cookie auth later without a rewrite.

nodes.label: Server-side SHA-256 Token Hashing & Revocation
nodes.rationale: Tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes, re-checked against the roster on every request, and revocable per browser from the /extension page.

nodes.label: connect.js content script (token relay)
nodes.rationale: Wrapped in an IIFE because every content script on the same document shares one scope, so a top-level const would collide with an identically named one in a sibling script and silently abort both.

nodes.label: background.js (service worker / event page)
nodes.rationale: Receives the pairing token and refreshes the cache every 15 minutes via alarms. Branches on IS_GECKO for async message replies: Firefox takes a returned promise, Chromium needs sendResponse plus a synchronous true.

nodes.label: lib.js (storage helpers + API wrapper + ext namespace)
nodes.rationale: Exports `ext`, bound to `browser` where it exists and `chrome` otherwise, so nothing else in the codebase branches on engine. Firefox 153 does return promises from its chrome.* alias, so this is belt-and-braces rather than a bug fix, but browser.* is the documented promise API.

nodes.label: build-zip.py (dual-manifest packager)
nodes.rationale: Writes both the Chromium and Firefox zips from one folder; every script is byte-identical and only the manifest differs. The Firefox manifest swaps the service worker for background.scripts, drops Chromium-only externally_connectable, and adds browser_specific_settings.gecko. Must be re-run after any change or the downloads go stale.

nodes.label: Cross-browser parity (Chromium vs Gecko, three divergences)
nodes.rationale: The two engines differ in exactly three places: the extension namespace, async message replies, and the background context (service worker vs event page). All three are isolated so no feature code branches on engine.

nodes.label: LAYORA_ORIGIN must agree in three places
nodes.rationale: Repointing at another deployment requires updating LAYORA_ORIGIN in lib.js, host_permissions in manifest.json, and externally_connectable.matches plus content_scripts.matches in manifest.json — a mismatch silently breaks the extension.

nodes.label: Known limit: a launcher added in the extension can be overwritten
nodes.rationale: Launchers live inside the single JSON blob the web app syncs wholesale. The extension write is a server-side read-modify-write and bumps clientTimestamp so an open tab picks it up, but a tab that already staged a write can still land it afterwards and drop the new launcher. Moving launchers to their own table would close the hole.

nodes.label: Known limit: a course without a link opens Layora instead
nodes.rationale: The course link is stored in the `platform` field (form label: 'Course Link (URL)'); courses saved with a plain label such as 'Self-Study' have no URL, so clicks fall back to Layora's courses page.
